items.title: Clark Terry interviewed by Joe Williams and Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, May 19, 1995
items.q: The interviewer mentions 'get Howard' in a narrative about going to a dance, but the interviewee (Clark Terry) does not respond with any personal connection, memory, or relationship to Howard.

ctx.x: Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah. Hot links and half smokes. And by the theater there, and then continued on down to get Howard, then continued on down. And we got there and that night all this Navy brass was there and it was an officer’s dance. And the old man sit down at the piano and started noodling, and finally opened up. And you know what he opened up with?

items.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Howard, down in Washington, D.C., yeah. He said to me, he says, “You know, dad.” He says, “You’re my man. I’ve been following you a long time.”

ctx.x: Yeah, for Minot. So anyway, we went to Minor, and we worked there for a while. And there was another band there named Herb Whitfield. He had a group working at a hotel. After this gig that Terry had folded, he sounded me and the bass player to come work with him, which we did. You know, naturally, you've got to keep working, and when you're poor you can't say no to no job. So we went on down there, and we started to work there. And I learned how to write for the... I knew the trumpet and tenor, I'd been writing…
What kind of things were you writing then?

items.title: 75230_Howard McGhee oral history interview
items.q: So we'd have Wardell Gray and Clark Terry, and several other guys that we liked, or that played well... All the people used to come out there.

ctx.x: somewhere along there. Anyway, a guy named Terry, who played piano, came to Grand Rapids to get some musicians. He heard the band was stranded there, and he came to pick up some musicians, because he had a job working at some restaurant in Minot, North Dakota. And he hired me and the bass player...
